problem_statement: uilibrary/matx-react (rebranded here as the Harbormill Operations Console) is a Material UI admin dashboard built with React and Vite that serves a single-page app to a static dist/ bundle: a fixed topbar, a left side navigation, a sign-in landing, an operations dashboard at /dashboard/default, and material worklist pages at /material/table and /material/form. Extend the console with a shared Operations Console Rail that rides at the top of every operations surface (the dashboard and the two floor worklists) inside the existing MatX layout shell. The rail is a compact, on-brand MUI Card band carrying three live shift signals (on-time dispatch, crew staffed, bays open), a 'Switch shift' toggle, and an active-shift readout. It must render through the layout on all three ops routes so the shift status follows the operator, must adopt the MatX Material UI surface/accent language (not an off-brand slate/amber panel), and its 'Switch shift' toggle must keep the readout in sync with the active shift. Separately, the existing Inventory Operations Gateway strip on the dashboard must stay inside a 390px mobile viewport without forcing horizontal page overflow. Leave all copy, tile values, DOM structure, and the rest of the Material UI shell unchanged.
required_content: A shared Operations Console Rail component renders through the existing MatX Layout1 shell on the operations dashboard (/dashboard/default) and on both material worklist pages (/material/table, /material/form), so the same rail appears across multiple admin routes rather than on a single page.
The rail shows a titled band ('Operations Console Rail') with three live shift signals (On-time dispatch, Crew staffed, Bays open) plus a 'Switch shift' toggle and an active-shift readout.
The rail adopts the MatX Material UI visual system (Card surface on the theme background, primary-accent left border, theme text colors) and does not introduce an off-brand slate/amber panel.

The rail's 'Switch shift' toggle flips between the day and night crew and the adjacent readout re-syncs to the active shift ('Active shift: Day crew coverage' / 'Active shift: Night crew coverage') after each toggle.

The Inventory Operations Gateway strip stays inside a 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal page overflow: the gateway row wraps or reflows to fit the screen while remaining visually intact on the 1440px desktop.

The topbar, side navigation, sign-in landing, stat cards, top-selling table, material worklist bodies, and the rest of the dashboard remain present and unchanged in content and structure. No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced.
design_constraints: Render the rail through the shared MatX Layout1 shell (route whitelist) so it appears consistently across the whitelisted ops routes; do not paste a separate copy per page or hang it off a standalone route.
Keep the rail in MatX's Material UI language: MUI Card surface on the theme background, primary-accent border, theme text/secondary colors, restrained spacing.
Do not introduce a new off-brand palette (no slate/amber recolor of the rail) or a new icon/chart library beyond the repo's existing Material UI setup.

The gateway-strip repair must live in the strip's own component styling and the rail's own styling; it must not depend on hiding overflow at the body/html/layout level or clipping content off-screen. The four gateway tiles must remain readable at every size.

The 'Switch shift' toggle must update both the active button state and the terminal readout together; the readout must not freeze on its initial value after interaction. Keep the Vite build pipeline intact so the app still builds to a working static dist/.
state_constraints: desktop_dashboard_top captures the operations dashboard at 1440px with the Operations Console Rail and the Inventory Operations Gateway strip both visible and on-brand.

mobile_dashboard_top and mobile_dashboard_mid capture the 390px dashboard: with the defect the gateway strip forces the document far wider than the viewport; the repair brings horizontal overflow within tolerance.
desktop_rail_shift captures the dashboard after clicking 'Switch shift' to confirm the readout re-syncs to the night crew.
desktop_worklist_table and desktop_worklist_form capture the material worklist routes to confirm the shared rail rides on those surfaces too.

The sign-in landing (desktop_initial, mobile_initial) fits its viewport with no horizontal overflow on every leg; all rail and gateway content must be inspectable as React DOM, not flattened into screenshots.

change_completion: A shared Operations Console Rail is added through the MatX Layout1 shell and appears on the dashboard and both material worklist routes.
The rail carries the three shift signals plus a 'Switch shift' toggle and an active-shift readout, and the toggle re-syncs the readout to the active shift after interaction.
The Inventory Operations Gateway strip reflows to fit a 390px viewport while keeping its four tiles, labels, and values intact.
design_consistency: The rail uses MatX Material UI Card, border, typography, accent, and spacing conventions and stays subordinate to the dashboard hierarchy.
The rail keeps the native theme palette and does not recolor into an off-brand slate/amber band; the gateway fix does not clip or hide content to mask overflow.
responsive: At 1440px desktop the gateway strip and rail lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
On a 390px mobile viewport the gateway strip wraps or flexes down responsively so the document width stays within the mobile screen with no horizontal overflow.
regression: Topbar, side navigation, sign-in landing, stat cards, top-selling table, material worklist bodies, and the rest of the dashboard remain present and unchanged.
No new console errors or failed network requests appear on any captured state.

author_notes: Repo-grounded modify/state_continuity/flow task on the MatX React Material UI admin template (React + Vite -> static dist/ SPA, rebranded Harbormill Operations Console). The L4 lever set rides on a shared Operations Console Rail rendered through the MatX Layout1 shell on a route whitelist, reusing MUI Card surfaces, the primary accent, and theme text colors. Four orthogonal discriminators: the gateway strip's mobile horizontal-overflow repair (no_horizontal_overflow); the rail's on-brand MUI palette vs an off-brand slate/amber recolor (visual_regression over the rail crop); the rail's cross-route presence on the dashboard and both material worklists (dom_assertions); and the 'Switch shift' toggle keeping the readout in sync vs a stale-closure snapshot that freezes the label (interaction_assertions). Firebase auth is stubbed to an authenticated demo operator and the app-shell overflow clips are relaxed to document flow as declared infrastructure, identical across reference/baseline/bad.
